content.text:
**Finding submitted — deviation (IP: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§2(d) (p0029)** is the only ownership provision and runs one way: TrueLink retains all ownership in the Interface. Vendor platform ownership is acceptable, but there is no mirror confirmation of our rights.
- No clause states that we retain **Client Content**, **Client's Intellectual Property** (p0011–p0012) or borrower/loan data passing through the Interface, and nothing addresses ownership of the **Support Services** results — while TrueLink's IP definition (p0017) captures "improvements... associated with the Interface," which could swallow work done for us.
- **§10** (p0063, p0065) only treats our data and the Support Services results as confidential, which is not an ownership right.
- **§8(d) (p0054)** grants TrueLink a broad licence to use, resell and exploit Credit Data — a negotiated bargain with a narrowed Credit Data definition, so I preserved it rather than reopening it.

Redline (validated, ok:true): new **§2(e) Client Ownership** inserted after §2(d) — we retain all rights in Client Content, Client IP, the Web Site and data through the Interface; TrueLink assigns the Support Services work product with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back for its embedded pre-existing IP; no joint ownership; §8(d) carve-out preserved. The comment offers the fallback (vendor keeps generic tools/know-how against a perpetual licence to us).
